En <b>Mis bibliotecas</b>, la pestaña <b: In My libraries, the Keywords tab compares the library's vocabulary with the rest of the corpus. With Speech only (ticked by default) it analyses only the speakers' prose: it excludes voting lists, the record's narrative, annotations, tables, notes and page headers, and the table shows how many words are left out; untick it to analyse the complete speeches. TTR is the proportion of distinct terms to words: it falls as the library grows, so compare only libraries of similar size. Keyness G² (Dunning's log-likelihood) measures whether a term appears in the library more often than expected: only terms with G² ≥ 10.83 (p < 0.001) and at least 5 occurrences are listed, excluding stopwords. The log-ratio is the effect size (each point doubles the relative frequency): Exclusive ≥ 6 or absent from the rest of the corpus, Very distinctive between 3 and 6, Significant below 3. With thousands of terms tested at once, pay more attention to the log-ratio than to G². A click on a term searches for it in Words mode within the library; Export table downloads the CSV.
